title: From Blind Spots to Gains: Diagnostic-Driven Iterative Training for Large Multimodal Models
claim: Prior self-evolution lacks diagnostics and diverse data, giving unstable gains on long-tail tasks; ours diagnoses weaknesses and adapts data, improving steadily.
layout: 2 panels: left schematic prior vs ours, right 2x2 line plots
description: Panel (a) puts two boxed schematics side by side. The left one, labeled VisPlay, shows a card stack reading 'Limited Static Vision Content'. Below it a confused cartoon robot points at question-marked bubbles (Artistic, Math, Medical), with a red loop labeled 'Unstable and Noisy Data'. The right one, labeled DPE (Ours), shows an 'Agentic Data Annotation' box with a retrieval/edit tool set, a robot, and diverse images. Below it a robot runs a diagnostic bar chart, and a green loop labeled 'Adaptive and Useful Data' feeds back. A dashed line separates panel (b). Panel (b) has four small line plots (HallusionBench, RealWorldQA, Charxiv, MathVision) across base, v1, v2 and v3. The orange DPE line rises steadily, while the blue VisPlay line is flat or erratic. Small robot icons show happy or dizzy states.
caption: Due to the lack of interpretable diagnostics and scarcity of visual diversity, previous self-evolution frameworks can alleviate hallucination to some extent but fail to provide meaningful improvements on long-tail tasks such as mathematics and OCR. As a result, the model often exhibits instability or even degradation in these capabilities during the evolution process. In contrast, our DPE framework effectively addresses these blind spots and supports a more comprehensive and balanced progression of the model’s abilities.
abstract: As Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) scale up and reinforcement learning (RL) methods mature, LMMs have made notable progress in complex reasoning and decision making. Yet training still relies on static data and fixed recipes, making it difficult to diagnose capability blind spots or provide dynamic, targeted reinforcement. Motivated by findings that test driven error exposure and feedback based correction outperform repetitive practice, we propose Diagnostic-driven Progressive Evolution (DPE), a spiral loop where diagnosis steers data generation and reinforcement, and each iteration re-diagnoses the updated model to drive the next round of targeted improvement. DPE has two key components. First, multiple agents annotate and quality control massive unlabeled multimodal data, using tools such as web search and image editing to produce diverse, realistic samples. Second, DPE attributes failures to specific weaknesses, dynamically adjusts the data mixture, and guides agents to generate weakness focused data for targeted reinforcement. Experiments on Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct show stable, continual gains across eleven benchmarks, indicating DPE as a scalable paradigm for continual LMM training under open task distributions. Our code, models, and data are publicly available at https://github.com/hongruijia/DPE.
